clue.text: A restriction against marketing of water

indicators.note: against means next to, so the pieces sit side by side in the answer

parts.note: a dam restricts the flow of a river
a sale is the marketing of goods

explanation.surface: A ban on selling bottled water.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's ale is an old jocular name for plain drinking water, the only drink Adam had.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a traditional humorous phrase for drinking water.

clue.text: A large tree or small plant

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
a pine is a coniferous tree

explanation.surface: A gardener choosing between a big tree and a little plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link word: the wordplay is A, large and tree, and the definition is 'small plant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpines are small plants native to mountain slopes, grown in rock gardens.

clue.text: Copper has the last word about judgment

indicators.note: about means going round, so the last word is placed around the metal's symbol

parts.note: amen is said at the very end of a prayer
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman insists on having the final say in a judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman having the last word, but it is the chemical element; 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen discernment, the ability to make sharp judgments.

indicators.note: shocked suggests something jolted out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A delicate bust gives the French a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fine-drawn is subtle: drawn out to a delicate, nuanced fineness.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer of allegories is annoyed by a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: An MP (Member of Parliament) is a lawmaker, someone who makes laws.

explanation.surface: Wasting time at the snooker table.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter time is to dawdle aimlessly at small tasks; a snooker player pots balls into the pockets.

clue.text: Capital investment makes Pat a hero?

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters of the following words are made into something new

explanation.surface: Putting money into the capital turns Pat into a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is the head and an 'investment' is something one is clothed in, so headwear; the question mark flags this reading of a financial phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapsible top hat worn to the theatre is headgear, something the head is invested (clothed) in.

clue.text: Edward besets Asian head about store for gunpowder, say

indicators.note: besets means surrounds, so the name is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: Teddy is a familiar form of Edward

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word Asian is taken

parts.note: ca is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Edward surrounds an Asian chief who is sitting on a gunpowder store.
explanation.walkthrough: Gunpowder is a kind of green tea with tightly rolled leaves, not the explosive; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddy is a small tin for keeping tea, such as the green tea called gunpowder.

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red
to start is to jump back or recoil in surprise

explanation.surface: Someone flinches with embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird, so a flier.

parts.note: lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: A coin is linked to a back ailment and to pencil lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is an old name for graphite, the black carbon in pencils.

indicators.note: about means going round, so the colour is placed around the fighting

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red
war is fighting between nations

explanation.surface: Shame about a fight over an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a prize given for an achievement.

parts.note: needles are things that sew

indicators.note: start to means only the first letter of the word split is used

explanation.surface: Sewers split open where nobody wanted them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewers' looks like drains but is read as things that sew.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needless is not necessary, so not wanted.

indicators.note: about means going round, so the sitting word is placed around the vehicle

parts.note: a hen that broods sits on its eggs, so brooded is sat
a van is a vehicle used by tradespeople

explanation.surface: A thinker brooded over a delivery van.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned person, a scholar or intellectual.

clue.text: It is found on the beach and retained by a customer

definitions.text: It is found on the beach

indicators.note: retained by means held inside, so the word and goes inside the buyer

parts.note: a shopper is a customer in a shop

explanation.surface: Something found on the beach is kept by a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link word before customer; the definition is a description of where the creature lives.
explanation.definitionFit: This small jumping crustacean lives among seaweed on the shore.

clue.text: Priest introduced to smoother kind of amphibian

indicators.note: introduced to means put inside, so the priest goes into the smoother

parts.note: a sander is a tool that smooths wood
a lama is a Buddhist priest in Tibet

explanation.surface: A clergyman is shown a newt-like creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A salamander is a lizard-like amphibian related to newts.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Instrument Ray wrongly (8)': the anagram fodder is cut short; PSALTERY needs SPELT besides RAY (likely 'Instrument spelt Ray wrongly'), but no scan or reprint confirms the missing word.

clue.text: Cartographer of Offa's kingdom missed one peak

indicators.note: missed means left out, so the numeral letter is dropped from the kingdom

parts.note: Offa was the eighth-century king of Mercia, an Anglo-Saxon kingdom
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tor is a rocky hill or peak, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A mapmaker of an old English kingdom overlooked a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: MERCIA without I gives MERCA. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerardus Mercator was the Flemish mapmaker whose projection is still used.

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the zero follows the verb

parts.note: to prosper is to thrive
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare nobleman flourishes on nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero is the exiled Duke of Milan in The Tempest.

indicators.note: include means hold inside, so the dam goes within the weapons

parts.note: swords are weapons that can wound
wear is an old spelling of weir, a dam across a river

explanation.surface: Curses, which can hurt, include the word 'dam'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam' looks like a mild curse, but it is a weir, here in the old spelling once used for a river barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscenities are rude words used in cursing.

parts.note: a char is a cleaning woman, short for charwoman
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A cleaner takes a job as a ferryman.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is British for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Charon is the boatman of Greek myth who ferries the dead across the Styx.

indicators.note: misprinted means the letters are set in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A typo in a German accent mark is a frequent error.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mutual is shared or held in common.

parts.note: to mete out is to distribute
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An alien landing hands out gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is a body from space that enters Earth's atmosphere.

clue.text: Greedy person showing strong desire to keep only child

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the desire surrounds the child

parts.note: lust is strong desire
o.c. is an abbreviation for only child

explanation.surface: A grasping individual wants to keep a single child.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the crop-devouring insect, a greedy person consumes everything.

clue.text: You previously appeared in stockings in the orangery

indicators.note: appeared in means it is placed inside the stockings

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings
thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: In the past you appeared in stockings in the glasshouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a heated glass building for growing citrus fruit.

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East, the Orient

indicators.note: reflection reverses an image, so the encounter word is read backwards

parts.note: meets means encounters

explanation.surface: An Easterner, thinking again, meets with respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard or respect.

parts.note: fresh can mean cheeky, which is pert
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: Looking at a new bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, a thing that flows; the Ure is in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye is an opening or hole, as in the eye of a needle.

clue.text: One gets into trouble about a plant

indicators.note: about means turned round, so everything is read backwards
gets into means placed inside, so the single letter enters the trouble

parts.note: worry is trouble or anxiety
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone gets into trouble over a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: A inside WORRY makes WORRAY, and 'about' turns that whole word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a wild flowering plant with feathery leaves.

clue.text: One who argues peevishly with cleric about fish

indicators.note: about means going round, so the cleric is placed around the fishing word

parts.note: RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
to angle is to fish with a rod

explanation.surface: A quarrelsome man goes with a vicar to go fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrangler is someone who quarrels or disputes noisily.
